annotations.text:
MainCourse on the web — desktop and mobile, static mockups.

The agreed look: Direction A's layout, cards and chip filtering, wearing Direction B's skin — IBM Plex Sans + Plex Mono, cool greys, deep green #16624B with lime as the only signal colour, 4–6px radii. Light rail, as you picked.

Every screen artboard pairs the 872px desktop shell with a 360px phone.

You were right about the tab bar — it was a native pattern smuggled into a web page.

What replaces it: a top app bar with a menu button, and the whole left rail slides in as a drawer. Same nav, same cookbook switcher, same Collections — just disclosed rather than always-on. Sub-pages get a back affordance instead.

The cookbook switcher becomes a bottom sheet on mobile. Both are drawn on the Mobile navigation artboard.

Scope notes.

Drawn: recipes, recipe detail, search (results + empty), shopping list, cookbooks (members, invite link, and the create-one state), settings, import (link/upload/camera, in-progress, failed), sign in, Pro, invite accept, mobile nav.

Not drawn: Meal Plan — hidden in the iOS app, so out of scope here.

Photos are placeholder gradients. Longer screens clip at the frame edge where the real page would scroll.

Open questions worth your call:

• Search — kept as its own destination because iOS has it as a tab, but the ⌘K field in the recipes header may make the rail entry redundant on desktop.
• Shopping list tiles are 3-up on the phone, matching iOS. On a 360px frame the two-line names get tight; 2-up would breathe.
• Collections in the rail are read-only here. If tags are editable, that list needs an affordance.

The three first-pass directions, kept for reference.

You picked B's colour, type and radius and A's layout, cards and filtering — the merge became the design on the first page.

A — Paper & Persimmon
Libre Caslon Display + Libre Franklin, warm paper, persimmon accent, 2px radii.

Why: reads like a cookbook. Photos carry the page; the rail stays quiet.
Tradeoff: the serif and the near-square corners feel more print than product.

B — Mise en Place
IBM Plex Sans + Plex Mono, cool greys, deep green with a lime signal, 4–6px radii.

Why: a dense working tool — a dark rail, a command bar, a scannable table.
Tradeoff: the table hides the photos, and 128 recipes stop being browsable.

C — Night Kitchen
Bricolage Grotesque + Public Sans, near-black on cream, amber, zero radius.

Why: editorial and loud — a big headline, a feature card, hard edges.
Tradeoff: high style, low tolerance for long recipe names and dense screens.
